security_invariants.description: The active persona key and its valid NIP-01 signature are authoritative for baseline persona authorship; hints, repositories, caches, and optional Assurance cannot override them.
A writer NID enters a repository union only after owner authorization and the NID's Ed25519 proof verify over the same exact binding.
Every signed object is locally signature-verified and, where applicable, delegation-checked before rendering, storage, or authorization.
Core discovery does not depend on a centralized persona, npub, RID, or serving-node directory.
Persona nsec, NID secrets, and sensitive cached identity material are protected by the Core keys-repository profile, including NIP-49 wrapping where applicable.
Absent, invalid, stale, or withdrawn Assurance cannot invalidate a Core-valid active-key persona or alter NIP-01 or Marmot identity semantics.
Assurance attaches only when a cold-root inception and active-key acceptance bind the same exact active key, inception event, and cold-root signature.
Every succession authority proof, new-key acceptance, and witness receipt binds one identical digest containing every closed transition member except the proof signature values themselves.
A pinned Assurance state survives disappearing or conflicting hints and can be downgraded only by the active key plus current recovery authority.
A verified successor proves continuity but remains a distinct Nostr author and Marmot account whose authority does not silently inherit.
A compromise succession rejects Assurance authority at or after its effective cutoff and carries no subordinate continuation.

Succession transfers no succession authority, associated-key issuance policy, subordinate key, repository, group, delegate, financial, or application authority unless the record explicitly reauthorizes it.

Associated keys are accepted only for their exact head, active-key or epoch-threshold issuance ceiling, narrowed role and scope, issuer, subject, time bounds, active-grant proof requirements, and non-revoked state.
KERI export either preserves every security-relevant accepted Assurance semantic or fails without emitting a misleading partial identity.
Tier 3 content is audience-key encrypted before reaching any repository, seed, full node, or relay.
Tier 2 private repositories are selective-replication boundaries, not encryption, and clients present that trust boundary honestly.
Comms-owned non-key private state and audience or group material are encrypted under the Comms repository-encryption profile.
Cross-backend Comms processing runs on user-controlled clients; full nodes, repository relays, routing nodes, and Nostr relays are blind carriers for protected plaintext.
Feed, outbox, and delivery discovery do not depend on a centralized delivery directory.
Private mute, feed-preference, followed-repository, and other Social state are encrypted at rest using the owning Social or bound Comms profile.
Following, transitive discovery, and social-graph evaluation do not depend on a centralized follow-graph oracle.
Authorization and side-effect audit is encrypted and contains no replayable token or transcript.
A light client receives no persona, device, epoch, NID, repository, MLS-leaf, or agent-role private key.
Every privileged token is bound to the authenticated Marmot account and exact group.
Every privileged request uses current, non-conflicted private entitlement state and absorbing revocation.
A node-issued Control token is accepted only when its protected typ is exactly at+jwt, signature and issuer validate, time bounds hold, and audience is the exact issuing-node resource.
Mutation reservation precedes effects and cross-node retry is limited to provably safe cases.
An automated principal never receives or directly exercises a persona, epoch, NID, human-device, or agent-role private key.
An automated principal publishes only through the intent-level agent method, and raw signing, human-profile fallback, and attribution bypass fail closed.
Node-mediated Marmot operations expose only grant-filtered content and actions while all account, MLS leaf, epoch, and repository secrets remain on the designated node.
Epoch plaintext is erased and relocked before network or bulk-transfer activity.
Recovery access is finite and bound to exact identities, resources, direction, bytes, time, and completion.
Overflow SFTP uses a per-grant onion and isolated rooted process with Tor and SSH authentication.
Claim IDs, event signatures, issuer authority, typed references, and native proofs are verified before trust or authorization policy is applied.
Every delegated claim strictly preserves or narrows all authority dimensions and issuance chains contain at most eight edges.
Persona-issued device authorization is final only in canonical private claim-repository state, while authenticated reductions take effect immediately.
A valid revocation or authority reduction is irreversible, monotonic, and wins concurrent repository merges.
Private claim-ledger contents and decryption material are available only to active durable NID-bearing ledger readers.
Shared OIDC signing keys are separately encrypted and released only to nodes with active oidc-token-issuer authority.
A node mints only from a synchronized canonical checkpoint no older than the manifest bound, which cannot exceed 300 seconds.
HTTPS issuer metadata and the root-key-scoped Radicle continuity tree agree on the exact active issuer, keys, status digests, and authorized succession.
OIDC projection releases only claims allowed by scope, audience, client policy, consent, active repository state, issuer trust, and proof requirements.
JWT consumers enforce exact issuer, intended audience, time, signature, nonce when applicable, and token-type separation including typ at+jwt for access tokens.
Draft-21 status lists are signed, fresh, digest-bound across HTTPS and Radicle mirrors, writer-namespaced without index reuse, and never let VALID override other token failures.
A public-reader implementation consumes only verified Tier 1 content and never renders Tier 2 plaintext or interprets Tier 3 ciphertext as public content.

Every automated event uses the exact registered signer, key class, and optional association kind/value; an agent key is preferred, while a persona key requires the explicit OIDC persona-signing scope, and the event pubkey remains authoritative.
Every agent-authored application event carries the canonical automation attribution block at its tier-appropriate protected location.
Workload tokens, token identifiers, private source claims, and sender proofs remain confined to the protected authorization and audit boundary.
The pinned Marmot dependency remains authoritative for MLS, conversation events, encrypted media, and Nostr transport semantics.
The active persona key is the Marmot account identity, every device leaf remains independent, and neither Heterodyne continuity nor storage provenance aliases another account or leaf inside MLS.
Radicle storage and every Nostr or media interface preserve exact signed Marmot event bytes and encrypted media ciphertext.
Independent device leaves do not share secrets by default, and node-mediated clients receive no MLS, account, leaf, or repository secret.

Only a canonical Marmot routing commit by its active account-key administrator can authorize a routing binding and repository genesis with the same h, RID, routing-event ID, and authorized writer refs.
Retention expiry stops conforming advertisement and replication but never claims erasure of independent Git objects, clones, exports, or backups.

A trusted seed receives only routing metadata and exact encrypted event bytes, writes only its own active authorized NID ref, and gains no persona, repository-owner, group-admin, full-node, or MLS authority.

Every private seed read or write requires NIP-42 account authentication plus one unique current unexpired administrator-signed ACL head matching the account role, seed grant, h, private RID, and Marmot group transition.
Agent-policy receipts inform publicly, but only an explicitly subscribed and verified current policy list changes a client's local visibility.
Agent-policy enforcement and remediation target only the offending role device key; replacement at the same role address never requires epoch-key rotation.
Workspace affiliation alone grants no role or resource capability.
Child roles, resources, grants, and bilateral allowances cannot widen an applicable workspace or parent-role ceiling.
Public state reveals no stable identifier, digest, count, locator, or correlation for a concealed workspace, role, relationship, repository, or resource.
Git authorship, Radicle permission, relay acceptance, MLS membership, and host status are never sufficient Workspace authorization evidence.
Role MLS state authorizes delivery but never serves as one universal content key for subordinate resources.
Revocation blocks future authorization and key delivery without claiming erasure of data or keys already obtained.
Ordinary writes use checkpoints no older than 86400 seconds and authority mutations no older than 300 seconds, with policy able only to shorten those bounds.
Hosting does not grant governance authority, while key-custody hosts remain explicit confidentiality trust boundaries.
Every effective role retains an authorized Radicle locator and eligible Radicle-backed relay host independent of optional Nostr relays.
Each authorized device has an independently revocable MLS leaf and receives only device-bound resource-key envelopes.
